Regarding an economy, we need to look at what the currency is.

Suppose it's an in-game item such as Gold. Gold is, at multiple rates, farmable (even if you choose not to glitch yourself into the Nether Ceiling). Imaginary internet points (or more formal "money") must either be created regularly or else we lose money whenever a player with an amount over zero leaves the server.

It's painfully obvious then that we shouldn't look then at the availability of the currency as our primary factor, but rather examine how we want the resources in the shops to be provided. Minecraft is a video game, it doesn't need to answer to scarcity unlike the real world, therefore we could hypothetically have a shop with unlimited stock, making players that have farmed currency not have a significant impact on the economy. The downside to this is that it requires moderation of the server to set the prices or else it can be exploited by players. On the other hand, having players run shop out of their stocks, using prices that they set creating a capitalist system. The downside to this is the problem mentioned earlier of players farming currency, where economic inflation may occur (I can tell you for sure that this ruined a Lapis-based economy of a server I used to play on).

IMO: a combination approach is best suited, where player-run shops compete against a spawn shop that offers goods at a price that's by no means a bargain. For what is used, we have imaginary internet dollars (each player starts with 100) that can be obtained by selling goods for hilariously low prices at a server-run shop or from selling their own goods in their own shop.

It needs to be decided, do we want a currency system, or an economy.

If we want an currency system, than I would propose that you can sell un-refined resources, like iron, coal, wheat, milk, sugar cane. You can purchase refined resources, like armor, pickaxes, food items like break or cake. Seeds as well, for the farmer in all of us. This method would limit what players can actually use their cash for. Really, in my opinion, it's a pointless add-on, unless you add even more add-on(s) to support this system. As for the currency, it would make sense to use imaginary points. Not, for example, in game items such as gold nuggets. It is very very very easy to abuse a currency system, if the creators of said system are not careful. In my opinion, this system is just not very fun.

If we want an economy, than I would propose you can buy AND sell a large number of items. You create a market, and on creation set the number of each item that is in the market. Values of said items are not hard-coded. They are based on the number of the item in the market. This is really awesome IMO. You could have a flood of diamond pickaxes into the market, and a shortage of iron pickaxes. This would make an iron pickaxe more valuable than a diamond pickaxe, based on sheer volume. To prevent abuse of this mechanism, the rarity of the material is calculated, and how much of said material is needed to make an item. So now, if a flood of diamond pickaxes hit the market, it's reasonable to assume that there will be a small amount of diamonds left in the market, making the material of diamond pickaxes very rare and scarce, keeping their price high, while still allowing for the price to drop. If there is a shortage of iron pickaxes, it would be also be reasonable to assume there is a large amount of iron ingots AND ore on the market, keeping the price low, but still allowing the price to increase. So the market tends to balance itself out, but merchants can still make a profit or lose. Miners, Farmers, Fisherman, Warriors, and Alchemists all have a place to buy and sell their respective items, and purchase needed ones.

As you can see, the advantage of a SMART economy is pretty large. But it gets larger. The possibilities of what you can build off of this market are great. But first, what is used for the currency needs to be decided. Do we all agree a dollar is worth a dollar? Or is our currency backed by a natural resource? If we went with a resource backed currency, it would allow an active generation of wealth, but would be very volatile. It would be able to inflate very easily. Banks could be created - by players - that hold large amounts of the backing resource and effectively control the market and value of the currency. This method creates much more work for server mods and admins. If we say a dollar will always be a dollar, than we accomplish the objective of the market: trade resources and items. Generation of wealth is lesser, but I think it would be much much harder for this type of currency to inflate. In addition, it allows banks to be created - again, by players - to loan out the currency, hold items, provide safe trade zones, the list goes on. Hell, you could also see player owned towns spring up, creating a real estate market and offering protection from other players and mobs in exchange for a lot purchase and perhaps rental fee. Shops in these towns would likely spring up, offering items not on the market, such as a livestock, or easy access items - more on that later - that players normally wouldn't have. Players could offer services. For example, if I created a bank, than I would want to hire somebody to run security for me. Or, if I was travelling across the world, I would likely want an guard. I like the option, an economy, as it really adds much to server, much more than a currency system. People will get very creative with it.

So now, where is this currency held? I would say on the player. Perhaps make it similar to that of XP, where the player drops a percent of points on death. This way, PvP is still an option for players to make money. This would also make a need for players to create banks. Now, how does a player access the market? First, I think the best option would be a new UI menu that contains the market. Walls and walls filled with signs isn't fun, IMO. To access, maybe the player activates a sign, opening the menu. For this option, I would say there needs to be a central location, perhaps at spawn, where players access the market. This would add a level of danger: Travelling to and from the market can get you killed. This helps prevent players from sitting in their mine making a ton of money, building an underground castle. It forces players to interact with each other. It would also make sense to allow purchasing of a sign that allows remote access to the market. If a player town springs up and wants access to the market from their village, or a player does from their home, they can do so. If a central location idea is not popular, than make the market accessible by pressing a key, similar to opening the inventory.

So IMO, and Economy is better than a currency system. Let me know what ya'll think.

TL;DR Market-based economies are more complex, but much more fun and create greater possibilities than a currency system. Currency systems are easily abused, a market-based economy balances itself with proper checks and balances put into place. Make the currency for the economy carried on the player, perhaps like XP. A dollar is a dollar, the currency is not backed by a resource. Access through the market is through a UI menu, no massive sign walls.
